highlights: Dual-arm collaborative robot coordinates both arms for small-parts assembly
Manufacturer rates each arm for 0.5 kg payload and 0.56 m reach
Lead-through teaching and configurable grippers support assembly workflows

The 2023 named-model selection table gives 14 total axes, 38 kg including the integrated controller, 0.5 kg payload and 0.56 m reach per arm. The two arms are not treated as one arm with a doubled payload rating.

Maximum TCP speed is 1.5 m/s and pose repeatability 0.02 mm in the 2023 portfolio. Repeatability is not a universal absolute positioning or inspection-accuracy guarantee; actual collaborative operation requires an application risk assessment.

The table lists IP30, ISO Clean Room 5, table mounting and IRC5 integrated into the body for dual-arm YuMi. Its Category B, PL b safety entry remains distinct from IRB 14050’s Category 3, PL d; the brochure’s no-fence language is qualified by the absence of hazardous tools/workpieces.

Lead-through teaching and configurable servo/vacuum/vision SmartGripper tooling are described. Wizard easy programming is explicitly marked for single-arm YuMi only in the YuMi spread, so it is not assumed for IRB 14000. The 2023 copyright is not a launch date or evidence of current availability.

IP40 is standard and IP67 optional in the 2023 table, not IP67 for every robot. The column also lists ISO Clean Room 4, Category 3, PL d, OmniCore and any-angle mounting. Protection/cleanroom claims do not extend automatically to the installed tooling or complete cell.

Maximum TCP speed is not universal safe collaborative speed; an application risk assessment is required. Wizard, external lead-through tooling, integrated air and status lights are integration features, not additional robot identities.

companyFocuses.name: ABB Robotics
companyFocuses.role: Industrial robot and collaborative-arm manufacturer; selected 2023 YuMi, GoFa and SWIFTI portfolio reviewed, with controls/tooling/software separated
highlights: The 2023 collaborative portfolio separately names dual-arm YuMi IRB 14000, single-arm YuMi IRB 14050, GoFa 5/10/12 CRB 15000 and SWIFTI CRB 1100/1300. This selected cobot review does not establish ABB’s full industrial, mobile, painting, delta or historical robot portfolio.

Dual-arm YuMi has 14 total axes, 38 kg including IRC5 and 0.5 kg/0.56 m per arm. Single-arm YuMi has seven axes, 9.6 kg and 0.5 kg/0.56 m, with OmniCore. The table’s Category B, PL b versus Category 3, PL d entries and cleanroom Classes 5 versus 6 remain distinct.

The 2023 GoFa configurations list 5/10/12 kg payloads, reaches 1.05/1.62 TCP/1.37 m and masses 28/51/48 kg in their separate columns. Each has six axes, integrated joint torque sensing and 0.02 mm pose repeatability. These dated values do not establish later revisions or current availability.

GoFa 5 is listed IP54 and GoFa 10 IP67. GoFa 12’s source cell literally reads IP567, so its numeric IP field is omitted pending a reliable model-specific source. The typo is not silently corrected or transferred from another configuration.

SWIFTI CRB 1100 lists 4 kg, 21 kg and 0.01 mm repeatability; CRB 1300 lists 7/10/11 kg, 75/77/79 kg and 0.02 mm. Their multiple reach/speed/payload/mass entries remain family arrays without inferred exact variant pairing. CRB 1300 IP40 standard and IP67 optional remain distinct.

GoFa lead-through uses integrated torque sensing; SWIFTI uses an external teaching device and SafeMove/safety-sensor supervision that stops before contact. Maximum TCP speeds are not universal safe collaborative speeds. Hazardous tools/workpieces and application-specific risk assessments qualify broad no-fence marketing.

Wizard is explicitly single-arm-only in the YuMi spread. IRC5/OmniCore controllers, SmartGripper/vision/vacuum tooling, RobotStudio/Wizard software, service monitoring and AGV mounting have separate roles. Brochure copyright, 1974 company history and 24/7 diagnostics are not model release, battery duration or continuous-duty ratings; exclusive USPs and leadership remain unproven.
